traits.notes: Multiple images show the same seedling with five leaves arranged in a whorl at the top of the stem. Some leaves have minor damage, including small holes and margin irregularities, but these are not extensive. The leaf margins are consistently serrate, and the surface has fine trichomes. The stem is woody with a ridged texture and fine hairs. No stipules, latex, or pulvinus are visible. The overall growth form is compact and low-growing, typical of a young seedling in a shaded forest floor environment. The leaf shape is lanceolate with an acute apex and cuneate base. Secondary veins are prominent and closely spaced, contributing to the rugose surface texture.

A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (five leaves clearly attached at a single node, visible in multiple images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped tightly at the node, with no visible internodes between them)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade, not divided into leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A

    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (longer than wide, tapering to a pointed apex, widest near the base)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (sharply pointed tip, not drawn out into a long tail)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (wedge-shaped, tapering to the petiole)

    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): dull, rugose (surface is not shiny; has a slightly wrinkled or textured appearance)

    19. Stem color: brown (stem is dark brown with a slightly rough texture)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): ridged (stem surface has slight longitudinal ridges and grooves)
